Sezgen, O. and Koomey, J.G. (1995). Technology Data Characterizing Water Heating in Commercial Buildings: Application to End-Use Forecasting. Report LBL-37398 (UC-1600), Ernest Orlando Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Berkeley, CA, December 1995. No DOI printed.

29-page report on commercial-building water heating for the COMMEND end-use forecasting model; locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 4 or so; the report has roman-numeral front matter). Commercial buildings are out of scope; only equipment that is also heat-supply equipment was loaded: water-heating plant Tables 7-11 (storage tanks, tanks heated by space-heating boilers, tankless coils, residential-type storage, point-of-use) with annual efficiency, service life, size and 1992-dollar cost where printed. Recovery efficiency is in other-values. Not loaded: service demand, distribution systems (insulation, pipes), saturations, building prototypes. Traps: (1) costs are 1992 dollars (1990 converted with 1.073); (2) Table 7 costs for measures are INCREMENTAL over baseline and have two components (per gallon of storage plus per kBtu/h or kW input) given as two capex rows; baseline cost not printed; (3) Table 8/9 costs exclude the boiler; (4) annual efficiencies include standby losses and a heating vs cooling season split for boiler-heated tanks; (5) heat pump efficiencies are printed as percentages above 100 (COP x 100); (6) Table 10 costs are for the complete option, not incremental; (7) no heating-value basis stated. All rows mapped (none) or low: no industrial archetype matches building water heaters.
